rule.description: A maximal group of loose named parameters (at least 4 shared names) that recurs member-for-member in at least 3 function signatures spread over at least 2 production files. Signatures containing the recurring group (or a qualifying 4+-name subset) are flagged as carriers; non-carrier call sites forwarding at least 3 member-named arguments into other functions are flagged as shredding call-sites where a cohesive data group is taken apart. Destructured and rest parameters count as one opaque slot and never participate.

checks.description: Function signatures that enumerate a recurring group of loose subscription connection/parse parameters member-for-member (url, username, password, obfuscation, format, applyProxy, success, fail, or a qualifying 4+-name subset such as obfuscation/format/success/fail).
checks.detected_relation: recurring loose parameter group -> [url, username, password, obfuscation, format, applyProxy, success, fail] across signature carriers in 3 files
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: A cohesive subscription request configuration (plus the callback pair that always accompanies it) is spelled out as independent parameters in signature after signature instead of traveling as one value; the maximal recurring group spans the proxy-server reader, the rules reader and the shared transport in three different modules.

matches.evidence: readFromServer(url, username, password, obfuscation, format, applyProxy, proxyProtocol, success?, fail?) carries all 8 recurring member names (line 25 in the injected state).
readFromServerAndImport(url, username, password, obfuscation, format, applyProxy, success?, fail?) repeats the full recurring group (line 31 in the injected state).

The shared transport signature fetchSubscriptionText(url, username, password, obfuscation, format, applyProxy, success, fail) carries the full group although its body only reads url, username, password and applyProxy - obfuscation and format are forwarded dead weight (line 28 in the injected state).

importRulesBatch(obfuscation, format, text, file, noDuplicates, currentRules, success, fail?) leads with the parse subset (obfuscation, format) of the same group and repeats the qualifying member names {obfuscation, format, success, fail} (line 97 in the injected state).

importText(text, file, append, currentProxies, success, fail?, obfuscation?, format?, proxyProtocol?) trails with the parse subset (obfuscation, format, proxyProtocol) and repeats the qualifying member names {obfuscation, format, success, fail} (line 88 in the injected state).

checks.description: Non-carrier call sites that take a cohesive stored subscription (or editor-bound subscription model) apart and forward its connection fields as individual arguments into the carrier readers.
checks.detected_relation: stored subscription object -> per-field forwarding -> carrier signature (readFromServer / readFromServerAndImport)
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The data group is decomposed into loose pieces precisely at the boundary where a single value should be handed over; server-side sites forward [url, username, password, obfuscation, format, applyProxy ( proxyProtocol outside the recurring core)] and rules-side sites forward the six recurring members. These sites exist in both the scheduled background refresh lifecycle and the settings UI save/test flows.

matches.evidence: Timer-driven server-subscription refresh forwards subscription.url, subscription.username, subscription.password, subscription.obfuscation, subscription.format, subscription.applyProxy (plus subscription.proxyProtocol) into ProxyImporter.readFromServer (line 171 in the injected state).

Timer-driven rules-subscription refresh forwards subscription.url, subscription.username, subscription.password, subscription.obfuscation, subscription.format, subscription.applyProxy into RuleImporter.readFromServerAndImport (line 360 in the injected state).
The save handler explodes subscriptionModel.url, .username, .password, .obfuscation, .format, .applyProxy (plus .proxyProtocol) into ProxyImporter.readFromServer (line 3714 in the injected state).

Inside the special-request round-trip of the test handler, the call forwards the same six subscriptionModel fields (plus .proxyProtocol) into ProxyImporter.readFromServer (line 3816 in the injected state).

The subscriptions-grid refresh button forwards editingSubscription.url, .username, .password, .obfuscation, .format, .applyProxy into RuleImporter.readFromServerAndImport (line 3981 in the injected state).
The rules save handler forwards subscriptionModel.url, .username, .password, .obfuscation, .format, .applyProxy into RuleImporter.readFromServerAndImport (line 4097 in the injected state).

Inside the special-request round-trip of the rules test handler (after applyProxy on the model was cleared), the call forwards the six subscriptionModel fields into RuleImporter.readFromServerAndImport (line 4223 in the injected state).

excluded.reason: The local rules import modal passes a literal null and its local sourceType/text/file values; it forwards at most one recurring member name, below the shredding threshold. It is a coupled call-site of the smell's signature change but is not credited as a clump manifestation by this rule.

excluded.location: browser message handlers with (message, sender, sendResponse) across ~4 files
excluded.reason: Pre-existing platform callback trio: only 3 member names, never part of the subscription connection group, and structurally a fixed platform callback contract rather than a recurring data group.

These receive at most 3 of the member names (proxyListText, obfuscation, proxyProtocol or proxyListText, obfuscation); fewer than 4 shared names, so no qualifying group can be carried. They are propagation endpoints of the loose-field threading, not credited carriers.
A leaf consumer registering one url/mode pair for a single request; only 2 shared names with the group and it is the intended endpoint of those two values.

excluded.location: subscription persistence paths (SettingsOperation, definitions CopyFrom, subscription grid rendering)
excluded.reason: These already move whole subscription objects end-to-end and never decompose them; nothing for this rule to detect.
